instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines "lobbyist" as an individual who "contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses, from a principal" — any economic consideration triggers lobbyist status with no dollar threshold.

The lobbyist definition in §13.62(11) is based on receiving economic consideration from a principal and on days of lobbying communication, not on the lobbyist's own expenditures; no lobbyist-side expenditure standard exists.

Itemization by name/address/amount of payments to a lobbyist is required only "If the total amount of lobbying expenditures and obligations... made or incurred to any lobbyist for the principal exceeds $200 during the reporting period," establishing a $200 per-lobbyist itemization threshold.

A principal anticipating aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations not exceeding $500 in a calendar year may file a verified statement and is exempt from licensing, registration, and reporting requirements; §13.64(1) likewise triggers registration only when expenditures exceed $500.

No statute establishes a percentage-of-compensated-time threshold exempting a lobbyist from filing; §13.62(11) uses a 5-day count for lobbyist status, and §13.68(1)(a)'s 10-hour rule governs whether a principal must include a non-lobbyist employee's expenses in its aggregate report, not a lobbyist filing exemption.

content.text:
I'll analyze each cell based on the Wisconsin statute text provided.

**row_001**: §13.62(11) defines "lobbyist" as an individual who receives economic consideration (other than reimbursement for actual expenses) from a principal. There's no dollar threshold — any economic consideration counts.

**row_002**: No lobbyist-side expenditure threshold for being defined as a lobbyist. The $500 threshold in §13.64(1) applies to principals, not lobbyists.

**row_003**: §13.62(11) — if duties aren't exclusively lobbying, the individual is a lobbyist only if they make lobbying communications on at least 5 days within a reporting period.

**row_004**: §13.68(1)(a)6 requires listing lobbyists who received >$200 in expenditures; §13.68(1)(a)5 has a $500 threshold for paid advertising aggregation. The itemization threshold for individual lobbyist payments is $200.

**row_005**: §13.621(5) — principals anticipating ≤$500 in lobbying expenditures per calendar year may file a verified statement and are exempt from full registration/reporting. §13.64(1) confirms the $500 threshold.

**row_006**: §13.68(1)(a) excludes from aggregate reporting employees who devote ≤10 hours to lobbying in a reporting period — but this is about itemized inclusion, not a lobbyist filing exemption. There is no percentage-of-time threshold for lobbyist filing exemption in the statute.

input.justification: The statute defines "lobbyist" as an individual who "contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses, from a principal" — any economic consideration triggers lobbyist status with no dollar threshold.

The lobbyist definition in §13.62(11) is based on receiving economic consideration from a principal and on days of lobbying communication, not on the lobbyist's own expenditures; no lobbyist-side expenditure standard exists.

If an individual's duties on behalf of a principal are not limited exclusively to lobbying, the individual is a lobbyist only if he or she makes lobbying communications on each of at least 5 days within a reporting period.

Itemization by name/address/amount of payments to a lobbyist is required only "If the total amount of lobbying expenditures and obligations... made or incurred to any lobbyist for the principal exceeds $200 during the reporting period," establishing a $200 per-lobbyist itemization threshold.

A principal anticipating aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations not exceeding $500 in a calendar year may file a verified statement and is exempt from licensing, registration, and reporting requirements; §13.64(1) likewise triggers registration only when expenditures exceed $500.

No statute establishes a percentage-of-compensated-time threshold exempting a lobbyist from filing; §13.62(11) uses a 5-day count for lobbyist status, and §13.68(1)(a)'s 10-hour rule governs whether a principal must include a non-lobbyist employee's expenses in its aggregate report, not a lobbyist filing exemption.
